summary: Suspected automated account enumeration followed by spike of external-invite accepts
description: Issue summary: Over a ~90 minute window multiple internal identities and service account acceptances of externally-sent onboarding invites were recorded immediately following a high-rate scan of possible usernames against our SSO endpoint. Impact: Potential account enumeration followed by unauthorized accept of external invites which could enable lateral access or automated attacker footholds. We are treating this as a security incident and triaging with SRE/Identity teams.
impact: 20 invite-accept events across 14 internal accounts (non-admin) and 3 service account key uses from unusual IP blocks within a 1.5 hour window. No confirmed privilege escalation observed so far. Some invite-accept events correlate with failed password resets and unusual user agents.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Monitor SSO /authn endpoint for a high-volume POST pattern to /idp/validate with many different usernames
2) Observe if SCIM provisioning/webhook trigger fires external-invite flow and invites are accepted from identical or proxied IPs
3) Check for subsequent service-account token exchange or API calls from those identities
logs: 2026-03-12T14:02:21Z - auth: POST /idp/validate user=bjensen@redwood.ai ip=45.76.12.9 ua=python-requests/2.27.1 status=200 latency=85ms
2026-03-12T14:03:07Z - invite: PUT /v1/invites/accept user=bjensen@redwood.ai ip=104.244.76.12 ua=Mozilla/5.0 (Windows) status=204
2026-03-12T14:10:12Z - audit: service_key use service=backup-agent user=svc-backup-01 ip=138.68.22.45 action=token-exchange
investigation_notes: Initial detection: automated alert from internal anomaly rule (high failed auth rate + invite-accept spike) at 14:05 UTC.
Identity logs show a burst of /idp/validate requests from ~45.76.12.0/24 and 104.244.76.0/24 which correlate to cloud provider IPs and possible proxy pools.

SCIM logs show external vendor invites created by our onboarding automation within seconds of the enumeration requests; invites were accepted from different IPs (residential proxy ranges) with consistent browser UA strings.
Cross-checked with Okta SSO: no admin console access, MFA challenges triggered for two users and were answered incorrectly multiple times; no successful admin-level actions detected.
Service account activity: three short-lived token-exchange actions occurred; tokens used for low-scope API calls only (read-only list endpoints). We rotated the associated keys as precaution.

Hypothesis: An automated script enumerated likely usernames, triggered an onboarding automation (SCIM/third-party vendor) to generate invites, and a separate actor or automated acceptor accepted invites to create accessible identities. Likely opportunistic, low privilege.
No evidence of lateral movement to sensitive resources found in the first-pass logs; timeline correlation still in progress.
actions_taken: Disabled external-invite acceptance for 2 hours to block further automated acceptances
Rotated three service account keys (svc-backup-01, svc-data-ingest-2, svc-legacy-sync)
Force-initiated password resets + revoked active SSO sessions for the 14 affected accounts
Blocked suspicious IP ranges at edge WAF (45.76.12.0/24, 104.244.76.0/24) pending further review
Opened a detection rule ticket to lower threshold for invite-accept anomalies
Notified vendor contact for the external onboarding tool to review webhook provenance and rate-limiting
next_steps: Complete full audit of SCIM webhook delivery logs and vendor-side logs (assigned to SRE-Vendor team)
Enrich logs with ASN/geo and submit to Threat Intel for potential automated proxy attribution
Add an automated pairwise check: if /idp/validate origin IP differs from invite-accept IP by ASN/mobile/residential signal then block acceptance
Prepare customer-facing incident summary if sensitive data access is later observed
Follow up with IAM to consider temporary tightening of onboarding flow (manual review for external invites)
